mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals a weakening supply chain that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) over the past 3 months signals persistent inflation that erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL has been rising over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1150 thousand units, it signals a contraction in the housing market that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when HOUST falls below 1150.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), strong payroll growth (PAYEMS > 150k) signals an overheating labor market that triggers Fed tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0 and PAYEMS growth exceeds 150k.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a 'stagflationary' environment that increases equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising CPI and falling FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
